options.label: Field dressing takes time
options.hint: When enabled, field dressing a kill takes game time (depending on animal size).

options.label: Skinning takes time
options.hint: When enabled, skinning a kill for its pelt takes game time (depending on animal size).

options.label: Harvesting takes time
options.hint: When enabled, harvesting a kill for bones and organs takes game time (depending on animal size).

options.label: Butchering takes time
options.hint: When enabled, butchering a kill for meat takes game time (depending on animal size).

options.label: Foraging takes time
options.hint: When enabled, foraging takes 1 hour of game time.

options.label: Scavenging takes time
options.hint: When enabled, Scavenging takes game time (depending on item).

options.label: Tracking takes time
options.hint: When enabled, tracking takes 15 minutes of game time.

options.label: Global time multiplier
options.hint: Modifies the amount of game time all Hunterborn skills take.

options.label: Include chickens
options.hint: Chickens require plucking in order to butcher for meat.

options.label: Include dogs
options.hint: Dogs require dressing in order to harvest and butcher.

options.label: Include hares
options.hint: Hares require dressing in order to harvest and butcher.

options.label: Include mudcrabs
options.hint: Mudcrabs require gutting to harvest. Gut them. Gut them all!

options.label: Include skeevers
options.hint: Skin Skyrim's skeevers!

options.label: Include slaughterfish
options.hint: Slaughterfish require gutting to harvest and butcher.

options.label: Click on fresh kill
options.hint: Action to take when "activating" a fresh kill.

options.label: Click fresh kill (sneaking)
options.hint: Action to take, while sneaking, when "activating" on a fresh kill.

options.label: Click on dressed kill
options.hint: Action to take when "activating" a dressed (cleaned) kill.

options.label: Click dressed kill (sneaking)
options.hint: Action to take, while sneaking, when "activating" on a dressed (cleaned) kill.

options.label: Pelt values
options.hint: How valuable (to merchants) are the pelts you skin from animals?

options.label: Material yield
options.hint: How many material components (like teeth, claws) should animals yield?

options.label: Meat yield
options.hint: How much meat should animals yield?

options.label: Custom meat yield
options.hint: As a percentage of animal weight; 12 = Conservative, 50 = Realistic.\nAnimals will always drop at least one meat.

options.label: Knives at merchants
options.hint: How readily available are hunting knives at merchants around Skyrim?\nChanging this setting will restock merchants.

options.label: Remove Manual Loot option
options.hint: The option for Manual Loot will be removed from the first menu on an animal carcass. Does not apply to Monster Hunter.

options.label: Prevent oversize stashing
options.hint: Large animals cannot be stored in containers. Because, c'mon, a bear in a barrel?

options.label: Prevent overburden pickup
options.hint: You cannot carry much more carcass weight than your encumbrance limit.

options.label: Prevent use in combat
options.hint: You cannot work on animal carcasses or use other Hunterborn actions (such as Forage) when in combat.

options.label: Require hunting knife
options.hint: You will need to buy or craft a hunting knife to effectively skin, harvest, and butcher a carcass; as well as for Scrimshaw.

options.label: Claws work as hunting knife
options.hint: Create hunter's caches as permanent storage. Uses Scrimshaw. See Readme for instructions.

options.label: Show screen blood
options.hint: Adds a blood splatter effect to the screen after working on a carcass.

options.label: Use animation for actions
options.hint: Plays a 3rd-person animation for actions taken on a carcass.

options.label: Use screen fadeouts for actions
options.hint: Screen fades to black for actions taken.

options.label: Enable Hunterborn Config Power
options.hint: Enables the Hunterborn Config Power. Uncheck to remove from Powers menu.

options.label: Enable Foraging
options.hint: Searches the surrounding terrain for useful materials. Level Foraging to unlock Bounty and Botany perks and improve Sense Direction.

options.label: Enable Scrimshaw
options.hint: A crafting system unique to Hunterborn intended to provide multiple uses for the bones you harvest from animal (or monster) carcasses.

options.label: Enable Primitive Cooking
options.hint: A new crafting skill allowing the player to sear meat over an open flame.

options.label: Enable Sense Direction
options.hint: Immersively discover the direction you are facing. Accuracy improves as you level your Foraging skill.

options.label: Enable Tracking
options.hint: Searches the surrounding terrain for game.

options.label: Enable Taxonomy
options.hint: Enable to add the Taxonomy ability to your spellbook. Taxonomy allows you to classify animals Hunterborn does not recognize. See the Readme for more information.

options.label: Enable Botany perk of Foraging
options.hint: Allows the player to learn extra effects from ingredients by consuming them. This works identically to the Alchemy perk Experimenter. Improve Forage to level 4 to unlock the first rank.

options.label: Enable Bounty perk of Foraging
options.hint: Higher levels in the Forage skill add a chance to gather more ingredients from plants.

options.label: Enable Savage Arrows
options.hint: Attacks with bone arrows cause extra bleeding damage.

options.label: Enable Soups and Stews Crafting
options.hint: Adds a new dynamic crafting system that lets you mix and match your ingredients in whatever combination, instead of needing specific ingredients for specific recipes. Requires patch from installer.

options.label: How long soup stays warm
options.hint: Lets you set how long soup stays hot. Set to 0 for soup staying hot forever!

options.label: Field dress
options.hint: Optional. Map a key to field dress the targeted carcass.

options.label: Skin
options.hint: Optional. Map a key to skin the targeted carcass.

options.label: Harvest
options.hint: Optional. Map a key to harvest the targeted carcass for ingredients.

options.label: Butcher
options.hint: Optional. Map a key to butcher the targeted carcass.

options.label: Process
options.hint: Optional. Map a key to process the targeted carcass: skin it, harvest it, and butcher it all at once.

options.label: Hide abilities in spellbook
options.hint: Hides the Hunterborn abilities from your spellbook. Useful if you have mapped keys to them instead.

options.label: Hide Hunterborn menu completely
options.hint: This setting hides the Hunterborn menu from appearing on any animal carcass at all. Useful if you have mapped keys for every action. This currently does not disable the Monster Hunter menu.

options.label: Forage
options.hint: Optional. Map a key to forage.

options.label: Scrimshaw
options.hint: Optional. Map a key to open the Scrimshaw crafting menu.

options.label: Taxonomy
options.hint: Optional. Map a key to invoke Taxonomy on the targeted carcass.\nSee Compatibility for tooltip, more information in the Readme.

options.label: Sense direction
options.hint: Use this feature if you hide the compass with iHUD, and end up getting lost all the damn time. Does not work indoors, due to technical limitations. Accuracy increases with your skill in foraging.

options.label: Tracking
options.hint: Optional. Map a key to track.

options.label: Primitive cooking
options.hint: Optional. Map a key to begin primitive cooking.

options.label: Total cleans
options.hint: How many animals you have dressed. You become faster at field dressing, skinning, harvesting, and butchering, as this amount goes up.

options.label: Skinning level
options.hint: Proficiency: Novice\nYou're still learning how to make the right cuts at the right angles, letting the knife do the work and not mere brute strength. Many of the pelts you take will be of poor quality or even ruined, but even these are still of use in making leather strips for bindings and wrappings.

options.label: Harvesting level
options.hint: Proficiency: Novice\nOnly the crudest elements of the carcass are accessible to you, mostly bones. You're able to shape these bones into some simple, but useful, Scrimshaw artifacts.

options.label: Foraging level
options.hint: Proficiency: Novice\nYou're still learning to orient yourself in unfamiliar wilderness, and distinguishing useful forage from scrap. Much of your time is wasted even trying to pick out tinder that adequately burns.

options.label: Dress
options.hint: Example of how long it will take you to field dress a deer. This time goes down as your total cleans goes up. Smaller / larger animals take less / more time.

options.label: Skin
options.hint: Example of how long it will take you to skin a deer. This time goes down as your total cleans and skinning level go up. Smaller / larger animals take less / more time.

options.label: Harvest
options.hint: Example of how long it will take you to harvest from a deer. This time goes down as your total cleans and harvesting level go up. Smaller / larger animals take less / more time.

options.label: Butcher
options.hint: Example of how long it will take you to butcher a deer. This time is based on the animal's size (and weight) and your current Meat Yield setting.

options.label: Reset to
options.hint: Use this option to manually adjust your prior experience as a hunter. This will set your total cleans, skinning, and harvesting levels.

options.label: Enable Monster Hunter
options.hint: Monster Hunter adds options to take skins, materials, meat, as well as venom, blood, and treasure, from the monsters selected below.

options.label: Chaurus
options.hint: Chaurus provide venom, chitin, eggs, and meat.

options.label: Spiders
options.hint: Spiders provide venom, eggs, and meat.

options.label: Spriggans
options.hint: Spriggans provide taproot... not much else.

options.label: Trolls
options.hint: Trolls can be skinned and butchered; their blood extracted; their fat, eyes, and hearts can be harvested; and they may carry treasure.

options.label: Werewolves
options.hint: Werewolves can be skinned and butchered; their blood extracted; their eyes and hearts can be harvested; and they may carry treasure.

options.label: Dragons
options.hint: Dragons can be harvested for their scales, bones, and some optional parts; they often carry treasure.

options.label: Corporeal dragons
options.hint: Dragons can also provide blood, eyes, hearts, and meat.

options.label: Use custom pelts
options.hint: Enable to use the custom pelts added by another mod, when skinning.\nSee the Readme for details and troubleshooting.

options.label: Combine with Hunterborn pelts
options.hint: Skinning supplies the custom pelts, AND Hunterborn's pelt.

options.label: Use custom materials
options.hint: Enable to use the custom materials added by another mod, when harvesting.\nSee the Readme for details and troubleshooting.

options.label: Combine with Hunterborn materials
options.hint: Harvesting supplies the custom materials, AND Hunterborn's materials.

options.label: Use custom meats
options.hint: Enable to use the custom meats added by another mod, when butchering.\nSee the Readme for details and troubleshooting.

options.label: Combine with Hunterborn meats
options.hint: Butchering supplies the custom meats, AND Hunterborn's meats.

options.label: Enable Hunting in Skyrim Full Compatibility
options.hint: Disables Hunting in Skyrim's Skinning system, but allows you to still gain experience and the perks associated with HiS skinning.

options.label: Use Hunting in Skyrim textures
options.hint: Skinned animals will use the alternate textures from Hunting in Skyrim. Requires HiS 1.3.7+.

options.label: Use custom textures
options.hint: Enable if you use a mod that dynamically assigns creature textures, such as Automatic Variants. This prevents custom textures from disappearing after you Field Dress animals.

options.label: Reapply templates
options.hint: Reapplies the changes Hunterborn makes when first started, including animals. This may help if adding another mod has broken Hunterborn. You won't lose your Hunterborn items or experience, but it is not as thorough as a clean save.

options.label: Debug mode
options.hint: Adds debugging information to Papyrus.0.log. Use only for detailed troubleshooting, this can impact game performance.

options.label: (SOTW) Enable Spells and Powers
options.hint: Checking this box enables the Spells and Powers disabled due to Skills of the Wilds leveling system.\nSkills of the Wild will unlock these powers when appropriate Campfire perk is purchased.

options.label: (SkyRe) Remove Gatherer perk
options.hint: Checking this box removes the Gatherer perk, which currently doesn't work with Hunterborn.\nSee the Readme for important notes about compatibility with SkyRe.

options.label: (PerMa) Remove Gatherer perk
options.hint: Checking this box removes the Gatherer perk, which currently doesn't work with Hunterborn.\nSee the Readme for important notes about compatibility with PerMa.
